entries.note: DOI 10.1161/CIRCRESAHA.111.300367 is correct (PMID 23542898; '.112.' would be wrong). Quote verbatim in abstract. Phase I arm is healthy volunteers, so untested stands under 'patient results'.

PMID 25470695; 71-90% apoC-III / 56-86% TG verbatim in abstract. Same via juxtaposition (comparison_stated=false), as cf-cftr Ramsey 2011 does. APPROACH 84% verified (Witztum 2019 abstract). No registry record found for the 3-patient study.
Quote verbatim in Graham 2013 abstract; dose-response is monkey-and-healthy-volunteer, no patients, so untested is right. mg/kg numbers unverifiable at abstract level, as the draft says.

Verbatim EPAR p.41 (typo '300 mg/kg' real). EPAR also says monkey PD 'cannot directly be translated to man' and <10 mg/kg untested; 'same' rests on an applicant Emax bridge. Field fix: magnitude within_2x uses modelled 5 mg/kg; vs lowest tested 10 mg/kg it is off_by_2-5x.
Quote verbatim in abstract. EPAR p.42 confirms TG fell only in fructose-fed HTG rhesus, not normolipidaemic cynomolgus (13/39 wk). TG&HDL WG 2014 DOI resolves (NEJM).

'<500 mg/dL' sentence verbatim in abstract; abstract itself frames the LPL-independent point. Juxtaposed same, house-style consistent. Gordts 2016 (JCI), Bergmark 2024 (NEJM) DOIs resolve; Balance registry 2025-03-06 verified.
Quote verbatim in abstract; platelets indeed not mentioned at abstract level. untested stands.

DOI 10.1089/nat.2017.0666 resolves; quote and 'NHPs appear to overpredict' verbatim. ISIS 404173 = different target (T2DM, 62 pts, 200 mg/wk, no PLT <75K) so 'other' fits the mechanism-based definition; indication is irrelevant. Field fix: confidence high->medium, source_calls_it 'match' overstates (abstract states a severe-drop miss).

Verbatim EPAR p.43 (conclusion 2.3.7). 39-wk cyno 0-3-6-12-20 mg/kg/wk: thrombocytopenia deaths at 12 (1F) and 20 (table reads '1M, 1F'), sporadic very low PLT >=6, verified. Table 37: 15/32 (46.9%) <100K, 2 (6.3%) <25K verified. FDA transcript 55%/18 pts and 'no effect on platelet function' (p.95) verified. CRL does not change status: rule 5, and the model flagged the hazard. same + direction_only stands.

field_corrections: dose[2].magnitude: 'within_2x' -> 'off_by_2-5x' (or null). The 5 mg/kg monkey dose is modelled, not tested; the lowest tested monkey dose (10 mg/kg/wk) is 2.5x the clinical ~4 mg/kg. Status unchanged.

safety[2].confidence: 'high' -> 'medium' (abstract-only, hedged 'may translate'); safety[2].source_calls_it: 'match' -> record partial: mean-decrease match, severe-drop incidence 'miss' in the source's own words. Status unchanged.

safety[3].judgement: 'one thrombocytopenia death each at 12 and 20 mg/kg/wk' - EPAR tox table lists '=12: 1F (thrombocytopenia)' and '=20: 1M, 1F (thrombocytopenia)', i.e. possibly two at 20. Minor wording.
missing: siRNA arm absent although mechanism says 'antisense / siRNA': plozasiran (ARO-APOC3) PALISADE, Watts et al., NEJM, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2409368 (Crossref issued 2025) - TG lowering in FCS with no thrombocytopenia signal; no status change expected, but the context note/model fields should say the siRNA relied on the same transgenic-mouse/NHP models (preclinical DOI not verified here).

Safety, possible earlier year: the FDA EMDAC transcript of 10 May 2018 (fda.gov/media/131530, p.94-95) already sets monkey and human platelet findings side by side ('no direct platelet activation either in monkey or human platelets'). If AdCom transcripts/briefing documents count as FDA primary sources under rule 1, safety 'same' moves from 2019 to 2018. Under rule 1 as written (label/review on accessdata or dailymed) the 2019 EPAR is the first qualifying source, so no correction proposed.

registry_date for the Gaudet 2014 three-patient study: not found in a ClinicalTrials.gov search for 'ISIS 304801 familial chylomicronemia' (only APPROACH NCT02211209, results 2022-04-13, and the open-label extension NCT02658175, results 2021-08-26). null stands but is unverified rather than confirmed absent.

Efficacy: the EPAR (p.42) itself states the monkey-vs-patient TG comparison (HTG rhesus only; normolipidaemic cynomolgus unchanged) and would be a comparison_stated=true source for efficacy in 2019; the draft cites it only in judgement. Optional, no status change.
rule_questions: Healthy volunteers as 'patient results': Graham 2013 itself juxtaposes the Tg-mouse/monkey knockdown with a phase I in healthy subjects (comparison_stated=true). If healthy-volunteer comparisons are admitted, engagement and dose become 'same' in 2013; the draft kept untested. Rule needed.

'other' for a platform-class comparison (Henry 2017): the definition is mechanism-based, so a 2'-MOE ASO against a different target in a different indication qualifies on the letter, and I decided 'other'. But (a) the toxicity mechanism (2'-MOE platform) is identical while the pharmacological mechanism differs - the table does not say which 'mechanism' it means; (b) Henry's agreement is partial (mean decrease translates, severe-drop incidence over-predicted) - is partial agreement 'agreement' for 'other'?

Hazard predicted, incidence/severity not (safety 2019): monkeys flagged thrombocytopenia (deaths at 3-5x the clinical mg/kg) but no monkey study produced the 47% <100K / 6% <25K seen in APPROACH, and that incidence drove the FDA CRL. The table has no status for 'right hazard, wrong magnitude'; I kept 'same' with magnitude=direction_only because 'contra' requires a wrong prediction and rule 5 bars using the refusal. Rule needed if incidence misses should score 'contra'.

Primary-source scope: does an FDA advisory-committee transcript or briefing document on fda.gov/media count under rule 1 ('FDA label/review (accessdata.fda.gov or dailymed URL)')? Decides whether safety 'same' is 2018 or 2019.

Dose 'same' on a regulator's model-based bridge: the EPAR says the monkey exposure-PD relationship 'cannot directly be translated to man' and that no monkey dose below 10 mg/kg was tested, then calls the monkey PD 'supportive' via the applicant's Emax model. I kept 'same' (source_calls_it=scaling) because the regulator's own sentence states agreement, but a stricter reading scores 'untested' (no tested-dose comparison; clinical dose came from human titration).
